claim_evidence.quote:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) for the invoked general causal and maximal-development suppliers.

In Minkowski spacetime $(\mathbb R^{1,3},\eta)$ with metric
$\eta=-dt^2+dx^2$ and time orientation $\partial_t$, let $q:=(1,0,0,0)$ and
$0<\tau_0<1$. The time separation from $q$
([[lem-gr-time-separation-maximizers]]) is
$$\tau_q(r)=\sqrt{(t-1)^2-|x|^2}\qquad\text{for }r=(t,x)\in J^-(q),$$
and equals $0$ otherwise. Then the level set
$$S:=\{r\in I^-(q):\tau_q(r)=\tau_0\}$$
is a smooth embedded spacelike hypersurface, every causal curve meets it in
at most one parameter value, and every point of $S$ is the past endpoint of
a future-directed timelike geodesic segment of length $\tau_0$ ending at $q$, namely the radial
segment $s\mapsto r+\frac{s}{\tau_0}(q-r)$ for $s\in[0,\tau_0]$, where
$r=(1-\sqrt{\tau_0^2+|x_s|^2},x_s)$.

quotes.quote: 2.1 (Smoothness and spacality.) On the open set $U:=\{r:\tau_q(r)>0\}=I^-(q)$ the function $f(t,x):=(t-1)^2-|x|^2$ is smooth with Lorentzian gradient $(-2(t-1),-2x)$, which is timelike on $U$ (there $(t-1)^2>|x|^2$); hence its level set $\{f=\tau_0^2\}$, which is $S$, is a smooth embedded hypersurface with timelike normal and is therefore spacelike ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]], [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], [[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). [step 1.1, L2, algebra]

4.1 (Radial description.) For $r=(1-\sqrt{\tau_0^2+|x_s|^2},x_s)\in S$ the future segment to $q$ is $s\mapsto r+\frac{s}{\tau_0}\bigl(\sqrt{\tau_0^2+|x_s|^2},-x_s\bigr)$, which is a geodesic with timelike velocity of constant norm $1$, hence a future-directed timelike geodesic segment of length $\tau_0$ ending at $q$. Conversely every past endpoint of a future-directed timelike geodesic segment of length $\tau_0$ ending at $q$ lies on $S$. [step 1.1, L2, algebra] ∎

1.1 (The distance formula.) For $r\in J^-(q)$ the displacement $q-r=(\Delta t,\Delta x)$ is causal, and for $r\ne q$ the unique maximizing geodesic image is the straight causal segment, whose length is $\sqrt{(\Delta t)^2-|\Delta x|^2}=\sqrt{(t-1)^2-|x|^2}$ when the displacement is timelike; for nonzero lightlike displacement the value is $0$; for $r=q$ the degenerate constant-geodesic convention also gives zero; this is the Minkowski instance of the attainability and geodesy of maximizers in [[lem-gr-time-separation-maximizers]] clause (a). [given, L1, algebra]

Conversely every past endpoint of a future-directed timelike geodesic segment of length $\tau_0$ ending at $q$ lies on $S$. [step 1.1, L2, algebra] ∎

3.1 (At most one meeting along a causal curve.) Since $\tau_q$ is continuous and $g(\nabla\tau_q,\cdot)$ has no nonzero causal kernel on $U$, the function $t\mapsto\tau_q(\gamma(t))$ is strictly monotone along every causal curve segment contained in $U$; hence such a segment meets the level $\tau_0$ in at most one parameter value, and a causal curve segment with $\tau_q$-values straddling $\tau_0$ meets $S$ at least once by the intermediate value theorem ([[lem-gr-time-separation-maximizers]] clause (b), [[def-continuity-real]]). If a causal curve met $S$ in two parameter values, the subsegment between them would join two points of $S$ with equal $\tau_q$-value, contradicting strict monotonicity; if the subsegment left $U$ it would contain a point $p$ with $\tau_q(p)=0$, that is $p\not\ll q$; but $p\le\gamma(t_2)\ll q$ and push-up gives $p\ll q$, a contradiction ([[lem-gr-push-up-rule]], [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]). [step 2.1, L2, algebra]

claim_evidence.quote:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) for the invoked general causal and maximal-development suppliers.

Take $\Sigma:=\mathbb R^3$, $h$ the Euclidean metric $\delta$, $K:=0$,
$\Lambda:=0$, $\kappa>0$ and the vacuum sector of
[[thm-gr-smooth-maximal-globally-hyperbolic-development]] (no matter fields,
$T=0$); the constraint equations reduce to $0=0$ and are satisfied. Then
the maximal development of these data is, up to a unique data-fixing
isometry, four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime
$(\mathbb R^4,\eta)=(\mathbb R^{1,3},\eta)$ with the standard initial
embedding $j:\Sigma\to\mathbb R^{1,3}$, $j(x)=(0,x)$, and time orientation
$N=\partial_t$.

quotes.quote: 1.1 (Minkowski is a development of the data.) On $\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with $\eta=-dt^2+\delta$ the curvature vanishes, so the Einstein tensor vanishes and $G+\Lambda\eta=0=\kappa\cdot0$: the vacuum field equation holds ([[thm-gr-vanishing-curvature-implies-locally-minkowski]] records the flat case). The slice $\{t=0\}$ is a spacelike embedded hypersurface with induced metric $\delta$ and vanishing second fundamental form, since the unit normal $\partial_t$ is parallel; and every inextendible causal curve in $\mathbb R^{1,3}$ meets $\{t=0\}$ exactly once, by [[thm-gr-minkowski-cauchy-and-global-hyperbolicity]]: its time coordinate is strictly increasing and has range all of $\mathbb R$. Hence $(\mathbb R^{1,3},\eta,\partial_t,j)$ is a development of the data. [given, L2, algebra]

claim_evidence.quote:
In the flat vacuum development $M=(\mathbb R^{1,3},\eta)$ of
[[ex-gr-minkowski-maximal-development]] with initial embedding
$j(x)=(0,x)$, take $S_0:=\mathbb Q^3\subseteq j(\Sigma)$ and the standard
coordinate basis at each point. Then the recursion of
[[lem-gr-development-quotient-dense-set]] produces the countable set
$$D=\mathbb Q\times\mathbb Q^3=\mathbb Q^4,$$
which is dense in $\mathbb R^{1,3}$ and meets the initial surface in the
dense set $\mathbb Q^3\times\{0\}$; and the associated exponential family
$$\mathcal B=\Bigl\{d+B(0;r):\ d\in\mathbb Q^4,\ r\in\mathbb Q_{>0}\Bigr\}$$
(the Euclidean balls with rational centre and rational radius, because
$\exp_d$ in Minkowski spacetime is $v\mapsto d+v$ in the standard
coordinates) is the standard countable basis of the topology of
$\mathbb R^4$, so $M$ is second countable.

quotes.quote: 1.1 (One exponential step produces the rational points with nonzero time coordinate.) In the standard coordinates the exponential map is $\exp_d(v)=d+v$ ([[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]: geodesics are straight lines with affine parameter in flat coordinates). For $d=(0,q)\in\mathbb Q^3\times\{0\}=D_0$ and a rational vector $v=(a,w)\in\mathbb Q^4$ the point $d+v=(a,q+w)$ lies in $D_1$ whenever $v$ is timelike, i.e. $a^2>|w|^2$. Given $(a,b)\in\mathbb Q^4$ with $a\ne0$, choose $q:=b$ and $w:=0$; then $v=(a,0)$ satisfies $\eta(v,v)=-a^2<0$, so it is timelike, and $(a,b)\in D_1$. Every exponential step from a rational point using a rational vector remains rational, so induction gives $D\subseteq\mathbb Q^4$. Hence $\{r\in\mathbb Q^4:\ r^0\ne0\}\subseteq D_1$, and $D_0$ supplies the points with $r^0=0$, so $\mathbb Q^4\subseteq D$. [given, L1, L2, algebra]

2.1 (Countability and density.) $D$ is countable by the construction ([[lem-gr-development-quotient-dense-set]], [[def-countable]]) and contains $\mathbb Q^4$, which is dense in $\mathbb R^{1,3}$ by the density of $\mathbb Q$ in $\mathbb R$ coordinatewise ([[lem-q-and-irrationals-dense-r]]); hence $D$ is dense and meets $j(\Sigma)=\{t=0\}$ in $\mathbb Q^3\times\{0\}$. [step 1.1, L1, algebra]

3.1 (The basis.) The repaired abstract family uses translated rational tangent balls: here $\exp_d(B(a,r))=B(d+a,r)$. Since $d,a$ are rational, its centers are rational; conversely every rational center is obtained by taking $a=0$ and that center as $d$. Thus it is exactly the Euclidean rational-center family declared above.  For $d\in D$ and rational $r>0$ the set $\exp_d(B(0;r))=d+B(0;r)$ is the open Euclidean ball of radius $r$ around $d$ centred at a rational point with rational radius; the family of all such balls is a countable basis of the Euclidean topology of $\mathbb R^4$ ([[def-topology-basis-subbasis]], [[def-second-countable-space]]). In particular $\mathcal B$ as defined in the statement is a countable basis of the topology of $M$, so $M$ is second countable, in accordance with [[lem-gr-development-quotient-second-countable]]. [step 2.1, L2, algebra] ∎

claim_evidence.quote:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) for the invoked general causal and maximal-development suppliers.

Let the flat vacuum data of [[ex-gr-minkowski-maximal-development]] be given
($\Sigma=\mathbb R^3$, $h=\delta$, $K=0$, $\Lambda=0$, vacuum). Let
$M:=(\mathbb R^{1,3},\eta)$ with the embedding $j(x):=(0,x)$ and let
$M':=(\mathbb R^{1,3},\eta)$ with the translated embedding
$j'(x):=(1,x)$; both are developments of the same data (in $M'$ the slice
$\{t=1\}$ has induced metric $\delta$ and vanishing second fundamental form
and is a Cauchy surface). Let $\psi:M\to M'$ be the time translation
$\psi(t,x):=(t+1,x)$. Then:

**(a)** $(M,\psi)$ is a common subdevelopment of $M$ and $M'$, and it is the
maximal common development;

**(b)** the glued quotient of [[lem-gr-development-pair-gluing]] is
isometric, in a data-fixing way, to Minkowski spacetime itself, the two
embeddings being the identity and the inverse translation.

quotes.quote: 1.1 ($\psi$ is a data-fixing isometry.) The translation $\psi$ is a diffeomorphism of $\mathbb R^{1,3}$ preserving $\eta$, the time orientation and (vacuously) the matter fields, and $\psi\circ j=j'$ by definition of $j,j'$. Hence $\psi:M\to M'$ is a development embedding of the whole of $M$, and $(M,\psi)$ is a common subdevelopment ([[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clauses (b)-(c), [[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a)). [given, L1, algebra]

2.1 (Maximality.) By [[lem-gr-maximal-common-development]] the maximal common development $(U^*,\psi^*)$ contains every common subdevelopment, so $U^*=M$ and $\psi^*=\psi$ by step 1.1 applied to $(U^*,\psi^*)$ in the reverse direction. In particular $U$ has no boundary in $M$, hence no corresponding boundary points, in accordance with [[lem-gr-no-corresponding-boundary-points]]. This is (a). [step 1.1, L2, algebra]

[given, L1, algebra]

3.1 (The quotient.) By [[lem-gr-development-pair-gluing]] the quotient $Q:=(M\sqcup M')/{\sim}$ with the identifications along $\psi$ is a development of the data and the maps $p_M,p_{M'}$ are data-fixing development embeddings; here every point of $M$ is identified with its image in $M'$ and conversely, so the canonical map $M\to Q$, $p\mapsto[p]$, is a bijection and an isometry: its inverse is the map sending the class of $m\in M$ to $m$ and the class of $m'\in M'$ to $\psi^{-1}(m')$, which is well defined because $m'\sim\psi^{-1}(m')$ and because $\psi$ is a bijection. Both compositions with $\eta$ agree, so $Q$ is isometric to $M$ by a data-fixing isometry; the two development embeddings are the identity and the inverse translation. This is (b). [step 2.1, L2, algebra] ∎

claim_evidence.quote:
Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same data and
let $(U,\varphi)$ be a common subdevelopment in the sense of
[[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a). Let
$C\subseteq\partial U$ be the set of boundary points that have a corresponding
point (clause (c) of that definition), and write $\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$. If
$C\cap J^+(\Sigma)\neq\varnothing$, then there exists $p\in C\cap J^+(\Sigma)$
with
$$J^-(p)\cap\partial U\cap J^+(\Sigma)=\{p\}.$$

quotes.quote: 1.1 (An initial boundary generator.) Choose $p_0\in C\cap J^+(\Sigma)$. Because $\Sigma\subseteq U$, the splitting in [L1] gives $p_0\in I^+(\Sigma)$. If the displayed exposed-point property already holds, take $p=p_0$. Otherwise choose a distinct $q_0\in J^-(p_0)\cap\partial U\cap J^+(\Sigma)$ and a causal curve joining them. Achronality [L2] and the null-versus-timelike alternative [L3] make this a null geodesic segment. Parametrize its maximal extension $\gamma:(\alpha,\beta)\to M$ in the past direction with $\gamma(0)=p_0$ and $\gamma(1)=q_0$. By [L4] it meets $\Sigma$ once, at a parameter $T>1$: a crossing at $T\le1$ would imply $q_0\in J^-(\Sigma)\cap J^+(\Sigma)=\Sigma$, impossible. All points $\gamma(t)$ for $0\le t<T$ lie in $I^+(\Sigma)$, because they are causally after $\gamma(T)\in\Sigma$, are not on $\Sigma$, and [L1] excludes the past side. [given, L1, L2, L3, L4, choose, construct]

[given, L1, L2, L3, L4, choose, construct]

4.1 (Follow only the initial connected component of corresponding points.) Let $J:=\{t\in[0,b]:\gamma(t)\in C\}$. It is relatively open and contains $0$ by [L5]. Define $s:=\sup\{t\in[0,b]:[0,t]\subseteq J\}$; relative openness at $0$ gives $s>0$, and every $0\le t<s$ belongs to $J$. On the interval $[0,s)$, the curve $f\circ\gamma=\Phi\circ\gamma$ is a past null affine geodesic by [L5]. Let $\eta$ be its unique maximal geodesic extension in $M'$, with the same parameter and initial data at $0$. Local uniqueness and connectedness give $\eta(t)=f(\gamma(t))$ for all $0\le t<s$; equivalently the interval solution itself is a restriction of the maximal solution. Each such value is a corresponding future boundary point, and hence belongs to $K':=J'^-(f(p_0))\cap J'^+(\Sigma')$, which is compact by [L6]. No connectedness of the entire open set $J$ has been assumed. [step 3.1, L4, L5, L6, construct]

claim_evidence.quote:
Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ be a development of the given data in the sense of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (a), write
$\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$, and let $h$ be the auxiliary complete metric of
[[thm-gr-auxiliary-complete-riemannian-metric]]. Then for every $q\in M$ the
set
$$K_q:=J^-(q)\cap J^+(\Sigma)$$
is compact. Moreover $K_q=\{q\}$ when $q\in\Sigma$, and $K_q$ is empty when
$q\in I^-(\Sigma)$.

claim_evidence.quote:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]).

Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same
data and let $(U,\varphi)$ be a common subdevelopment in the sense of
[[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a). Write
$\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$, $\Sigma':=j'(\Sigma)$, $I^\pm=I^\pm_M$ and
$I'^\pm=I^\pm_{M'}$. Then:

**(a)** $\partial U\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ is achronal in $M$, and
$\partial\varphi(U)\cap I'^+(\Sigma')$ is achronal in $M'$.

**(b)** Let $p\in\partial U$ and $p'\in\partial\varphi(U)$ be corresponding
boundary points to the future of the initial surface. Then
$$\varphi\bigl(I^-(p)\cap U\bigr)=I'^-(p')\cap\varphi(U),$$
and for every $q\in I^-(p)\cap U$ also
$$\varphi\bigl(I^+(q)\cap I^-(p)\cap U\bigr)=I'^+(\varphi(q))\cap I'^-(p')\cap\varphi(U).$$

**(c)** Let $p\in\partial U$ and $p'\in\partial\varphi(U)$ be corresponding.
If $\gamma:(-\varepsilon,0)\to U$ is a future timelike curve with
$\gamma(s)\to p$ as $s\nearrow0$, then $\varphi(\gamma(s))\to p'$ as
$s\nearrow0$. Moreover $p$ has at most one corresponding boundary point.

quotes.quote: 1.1 (Corresponding points have the same side.) Since the initial surface is contained in the open set $U$, a boundary point $p$ is outside it and therefore lies in $I^+(\Sigma)$ or $I^-(\Sigma)$ by [L1]. A point $x\in U\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ is timelike reachable from $\Sigma$ along a curve lying in $U$ by [L3], so $\varphi(x)\in I'^+(\Sigma')$ by [L4]; likewise for the past, using time reversal and [L3]. If $p\in I^+(\Sigma)$, restrict all source neighborhoods in the correspondence definition to that open set. The corresponding point $p'$ cannot lie in $I'^-(\Sigma')$, because this is open and would give a paired witness with inconsistent sides; and it cannot lie in $\Sigma'\subseteq\varphi(U)$ because it is a boundary point of the open image. Thus $p'\in I'^+(\Sigma')$. The past case is identical after time reversal. [given, L1, L2, L3, L4, algebra]

1.2 (Actual interior past at a future boundary.) Let $p\in\partial U\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ and $x\in I^-(p)\cap I^+(\Sigma)$. The open set $I^+(x)\cap I^+(\Sigma)$ contains $p$ and therefore meets $U$ at some $y$. Short timelike geodesic segments ending at $p$, with all earlier points sufficiently close to $p$, lie in this set by [L5] and the openness of $I^+(\Sigma)$. Thus there are actual interior past points tending to $p$. Apply the same proof in $M'$ to $\varphi(U)$ and reverse time on the past side. [L1, L2, L3, L5, choose, construct]

4.1 (Limit along an interior timelike curve.) Let $\gamma:(-\varepsilon,0)\to U$ be future timelike with limit $p$. If $p$ were to the past of $\Sigma$, then for sufficiently late $s$ the point $\gamma(s)$ would lie in $I^-(\Sigma)$, and a concatenated timelike curve from $\gamma(s)$ through $p$ to $\Sigma$ would have both endpoints in $U$, putting $p\in U$ by [L3], a contradiction. Therefore such a curve can converge only to a future boundary point. Fix an open neighborhood $V'$ of the corresponding $p'$. By [L6] choose an open causal-convex $W'$ with $p'\in W'\subseteq V'$. The interior past-geodesic construction of step 1.2 on the primed side supplies $q'\in W'\cap I'^-(p')\cap\varphi(U)$, with $q'\in I'^+(\Sigma')$. Step 3.1 gives $q:=\varphi^{-1}(q')\in I^-(p)\cap U$. For all sufficiently late $s$, $\gamma(s)\in I^+(q)$ by chronology openness, and also $\gamma(s)\in I^-(p)$ by the first argument of this step. The second equality of (b) then gives $q'\ll\varphi(\gamma(s))\ll p'$. Concatenate the ambient timelike curves from $q'$ to this point and from it to $p'$; both endpoints $q',p'$ are in $W'$, so causal convexity places $\varphi(\gamma(s))$ in $W'\subseteq V'$. This proves $\varphi(\gamma(s))\to p'$. Reversing time proves the corresponding limit statement for past-directed curves ending at a past boundary point. 5.1 (Uniqueness.) Suppose a future boundary point $p$ corresponds to $p'_1,p'_2$. claim_evidence.quote:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]).

Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same
data and let $(U,\varphi)$ be a common subdevelopment in the sense of
[[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a). Let
$$C:=\{p\in\partial U:\ p\text{ has a corresponding boundary point in }\partial\varphi(U)\}$$
be the set of boundary points of $U$ that have a corresponding point (clause
(c) of that definition). Then:

**(a)** $C$ is open in $\partial U$: there is an open set $G\subseteq M$ with
$C=G\cap\partial U$.

**(b)** There is an open set $\Omega\subseteq M$ with $U\cup C\subseteq\Omega$
and a smooth map $\Phi:\Omega\to M'$ whose restriction to $U$ is $\varphi$ and
whose value at $p\in C$ is the unique corresponding boundary point of $p$;
moreover, for every $p\in C$ there is an open neighbourhood
$W_p\subseteq\Omega$ of $p$ and a smooth **local diffeomorphism**
$$\widehat\varphi_p:W_p\to M',\qquad \widehat\varphi_p(q)=\exp_{\varphi(a_p)}\bigl(d\varphi_{a_p}(\exp_{a_p}^{-1}q)\bigr)$$
built from a common interior base point $a_p\in U$, chosen in $I^-(p)$ when $p$ is to the future of the initial surface and in $I^+(p)$ when $p$ is to its past, and the
exponential maps, such that $\widehat\varphi_p=\varphi$ on $W_p\cap U$ and
$\Phi=\widehat\varphi_p$ on $W_p\cap(U\cup C)$. No isometry property of
$\widehat\varphi_p$ on the part of $W_p$ outside $\overline U$ is claimed.

**(c)** At every point $q\in U\cup C$ the map $\Phi$ preserves the metric, the
matter fields and the metric-selected connection:

1. $g'_{\Phi(q)}(d\Phi_qv,d\Phi_qw)=g_q(v,w)$ for all $v,w\in T_qM$, so
   $\Phi^*(g')=g$ on $U\cup C$;
2. $(\Phi^*\psi'^i)_q=\psi^i_q$ for every listed matter field $i$;
3. for all smooth vector fields $X,Y$ defined on a neighbourhood of $q$ and
   every $q\in U\cup C$,
   $$\nabla'_{d\Phi\,X}d\Phi\,Y=d\Phi\bigl(\nabla_XY\bigr)\quad\text{at }\Phi(q),$$
   equivalently the pullback connection $\Phi^*\nabla'$ equals $\nabla$ at
   $q$, where both sides are read through the invertible differential
   $d\Phi_q$.

**(d)** Every geodesic segment of $(M,g)$ whose image is contained in $U\cup C$
is mapped by $\Phi$ to a geodesic segment of $(M',g')$; a null geodesic
segment is mapped to a null geodesic segment.

**(e)** Let $S\subseteq U\cup C$ be an embedded submanifold of $M$. Then
$\Phi|_S$ is an injective immersion, hence an embedding onto its image, and it
carries the induced metric of $S$, its second fundamental form with respect to
any unit normal field, and the matter fields together with their covariant derivatives of every finite order along $S$ to the corresponding objects of $\Phi(S)$ in
$M'$. In particular $(S,\bar g_S,k_S,\psi|_S)$ and
$(\Phi(S),\bar g_{\Phi(S)},k_{\Phi(S)},\psi'|_{\Phi(S)})$ are identified by
$\Phi|_S$ whenever $S$ is spacelike.

quotes.quote: 3.1 (Openness and the boundary values.) If $q\in W\cap\partial U$, take points $q_n\in W\cap U$ tending to $q$ using a countable coordinate-neighborhood basis. Then $\varphi(q_n)=F_p(q_n)\to F_p(q)$. The limit cannot lie in $\varphi(U)$: continuity of $\varphi^{-1}$ there would force $q_n\to\varphi^{-1}(F_p(q))\in U$, contradicting Hausdorff uniqueness of the limit $q\in\partial U$. Thus $F_p(q)\in\partial\varphi(U)$, and the same sequence witnesses the neighborhood definition of correspondence. Hence $q\in C$ and $F_p(q)$ is its unique corresponding point. Each $p\in C$ has such a $W$, so $C$ is relatively open in $\partial U$. Define $f$ on $A:=U\cup C$ by $f|_U=\varphi$ and the unique corresponding values on $C$. Each $F_p$ agrees with $f$ on $W\cap A$. [step 2.1, L3, L4, algebra]

4.1 (Euclidean patching and common jets.) Use the open cover of $\Omega_0:=U\cup\bigcup W$ consisting of $U$ with map $F_0=\varphi$ and all admissible pairs $(W,F_p)$ of step 2.1. Index by all such pairs, so no arbitrary-index choice of one map per boundary point is needed. Obtain [L5] and a subordinate locally finite partition $(\rho_i)$ from [L6]; write $H=\sum_i\rho_i(e\circ F_i):\Omega_0\to\mathbb R^9$. Each term is extended by zero off its cover member; subordinate support makes the extension smooth. At $q\in A$, every term whose support meets $q$ has $F_i(q)=f(q)$, so $H(q)=e(f(q))$. Moreover fix one local extension $F$ near $q$. On the open set $U$ in each overlapping domain one has $eF_i=eF=e\varphi$. If $q\in C$, every coordinate derivative of their difference is zero at $q$ by continuity from $U$; if $q\in U$ the equality holds on a neighborhood. Local finiteness and $\sum_i\rho_i=1$ therefore show that every coordinate derivative of $H-eF$ vanishes at $q$: apply the finite Leibniz expansion to $\sum_i\rho_i(eF_i-eF)$. This proves equality of all jets at every point of $A$. [step 3.1, L5, L6, L7, construct, algebra]

5.1 (Retraction and local invertibility.) The open set $\Omega_1:=H^{-1}(T)$ contains $A$. Define $\Phi=e^{-1}\circ r\circ H$ there. It is smooth and agrees with $f$ on $A$. For a local extension $F$ from step 4.1, the identity $e^{-1}\circ r\circ e\circ F=F$ holds near $q$; chain and Leibniz rules and the common jets from step 4.1 give equality of all jets of $\Phi$ and $F$ at $q\in A$. In particular $d\Phi_q=dF_q$ is invertible. Restrict to the open set $\Omega\subseteq\Omega_1$ where $d\Phi$ is invertible; it contains $A$, and $\Phi$ is a local diffeomorphism by [L7]. For each $p$, replace $W_p$ by $W_p\cap\Omega$. The original exponential formula remains a local diffeomorphism there and agrees with $\Phi$ on $W_p\cap A$. This proves (b), without asserting that the different exponential formulas agree on exterior overlaps. Countable Choice supplies [L5]-[L6], while Countable and Dependent Choice also accompany the boundary-structure supplier [L3]. [step 2.1, step 4.1, L5, L7, construct, algebra]

The limit cannot lie in $\varphi(U)$: continuity of $\varphi^{-1}$ there would force $q_n\to\varphi^{-1}(F_p(q))\in U$, contradicting Hausdorff uniqueness of the limit $q\in\partial U$. Thus $F_p(q)\in\partial\varphi(U)$, and the same sequence witnesses the neighborhood definition of correspondence. Hence $q\in C$ and $F_p(q)$ is its unique corresponding point. 6.2 (Homeomorphism on the closure side.) The map $f$ is injective on $U$; on $C$ it is injective by applying uniqueness of corresponding points to the reversed common subdevelopment, and its images of $U$ and $C$ are disjoint because they lie respectively in $\varphi(U)$ and its boundary. Write $C'$ for all corresponding boundary points on the primed side. Symmetry of the definition gives $f(A)=\varphi(U)\cup C'$. Apply the local construction of steps 1.1-2.1 to the reversed pair. Near every point of $C'$ it supplies a continuous local extension agreeing with $f^{-1}$ on its part of $\varphi(U)\cup C'$; on the open interior, the ordinary inverse $\varphi^{-1}$ supplies it. claim_evidence.quote:
Let $(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same
data in the sense of [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause
(a), with $\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$ and $\Sigma':=j'(\Sigma)$. Let
$\varphi:M\to M'$ be a smooth map with $\varphi^*(g')=g$, with
$g'_{\varphi(p)}(d\varphi_pN_p,N'_{\varphi(p)})<0$ for every $p\in M$, with
$\varphi\circ j=j'$ and $\varphi^*\psi'=\psi$ (so $\varphi$ is a future isometric immersion fixing the complete data and matching every matter field).
Then:

**(a)** $d\varphi_p:T_pM\to T_{\varphi(p)}M'$ is an isomorphism for every
$p\in M$;

**(b)** $\varphi$ is injective, hence a diffeomorphism onto the open subset
$\varphi(M)\subseteq M'$ and therefore a development embedding in the sense of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (c);

**(c)** if $M$ is connected and $\psi_1,\psi_2:M\to M'$ are two such
data-fixing isometric immersions, then $\psi_1=\psi_2$; in particular every
data-fixing self-isometry of a connected development is the identity of $M$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]) for the countable atlases in (b). Let
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same
data ([[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (a)), write
$\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$ and $\Sigma':=j'(\Sigma)$, and let $(U,\varphi)$ be their
maximal common development
([[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (b),
[[lem-gr-maximal-common-development]]). Let
$Z:=(M\sqcup M',\tau)$ be the topological disjoint union with canonical
inclusions $\iota_M:M\to Z$, $\iota_{M'}:M'\to Z$, and define a relation $\sim$ on
$Z$ by: $z\sim w$ when $z=w$, or $z=\iota_M(p)$ and $w=\iota_{M'}(\varphi(p))$ for
some $p\in U$, or $z=\iota_{M'}(p)$ and $w=\iota_M(\varphi^{-1}(p))$ for some
$p\in\varphi(U)$. Let $Q:=Z/{\sim}$ with quotient map $\pi:Z\to Q$ and
quotient topology ([[def-quotient-topology]]). Then:

**(a)** $\sim$ is an equivalence relation; $\pi\circ\iota_M:M\to Q$ and
$\pi\circ\iota_{M'}:M'\to Q$ are injective, continuous and open, hence
homeomorphisms onto the open subsets $(\pi\circ\iota_M)(M)$ and
$(\pi\circ\iota_{M'})(M')$, which cover $Q$;
$(\pi\circ\iota_M)(U)=(\pi\circ\iota_{M'})(\varphi(U))=(\pi\circ\iota_M)(M)\cap(\pi\circ\iota_{M'})(M')$;
and $Q$ is Hausdorff.

**(b)** $Q$ carries a unique structure of a second countable smooth
four-manifold ([[def-smooth-manifold]]) making $\pi\circ\iota_M$ and
$\pi\circ\iota_{M'}$ diffeomorphisms onto open subsets; a unique smooth Lorentzian
metric $\bar g$, time orientation $\bar N$ and matter fields $\bar\psi$ on $Q$
making both maps isometries that preserve the time orientation and the matter
fields. These satisfy the field equations of the data on $Q$, and
$\bar j:=\pi\circ\iota_M\circ j$ is an embedding of $\Sigma$ with induced data
$(h,K,\psi_0)$, so $(Q,\bar g,\bar N,\bar j,\bar\psi)$ is a development of the
data; moreover every causal curve in $Q$ that is inextendible in $Q$ meets
$\bar j(\Sigma)$ in exactly one parameter value.

**(c)** $\Psi:=\pi\circ\iota_M$ and $\Psi':=\pi\circ\iota_{M'}$ are data-fixing
development embeddings of $M$ and $M'$ into $Q$ in the sense of
[[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]] clause (c).

The representing fields $N,N'$ themselves need not agree there. By steps 4.2-4.3, $Q$ is a Hausdorff second countable smooth manifold. Under Countable Choice, a subordinate smooth partition $(\rho_M,\rho_{M'})$ for its two-member open cover exists by [[thm-smooth-partitions-of-unity-exist-on-manifolds]]. Define $\bar N=\rho_M(p_M)_*N+\rho_{M'}(p_{M'})_*N'$, extending each supported term by zero. This is smooth, and at each point is a nonzero future timelike vector because the weights sum to one and the timelike cone is convex ([[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]]). otin\overline{\varphi(U)}$. Otherwise $z\in\partial U$ and $w\in\partial\varphi(U)$. If every pair of their image neighborhoods met, then for every open $V
i z$, $V'
i w$ there would be $x\in V\cap U$ with $\varphi(x)\in V'$, by the exact overlap relation. This would be a corresponding boundary pair, contrary to [L1]. Thus the classes have disjoint neighborhoods. [step 2.1, step 3.1, L1, L5, contradiction, algebra]

7.1 (The Cauchy property.) An inextendible causal curve in $Q$ has a maximal portion in any open member image that it meets. By [L4] that portion is inextendible in the member and hence meets its Cauchy surface, so the whole curve meets $\bar j(\Sigma)$ at least once. For uniqueness, the sets $Q^\pm=p_M(I_M^\pm(\Sigma))\cup p_{M'}(I_{M'}^\pm(\Sigma'))$ are open and disjoint, and $Q=Q^-\sqcup\bar j(\Sigma)\sqcup Q^+$: this follows from the member side decompositions and their agreement on the common subdevelopment by causal convexity and future cone preservation. The surface is closed since its trace in each open member image is the closed member Cauchy surface. Near any surface point a future causal curve crosses from the past side to the future side, and has at most one local parameter visit, by a spacelike slice chart and strict temporal-coordinate increase. Thus the set of surface visits in a compact parameter interval is closed and locally isolated, hence finite. If two visits existed choose consecutive ones $t_1<t_2$. The connected intervening image, which avoids the surface, must lie in one of $Q^-,Q^+$. Near $t_1$ it lies in $Q^+$, whereas near $t_2$ it lies in $Q^-$. This is impossible. claim_evidence.quote:
Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(Q,\bar g,\bar N,\bar j,\bar\psi)$ and the
family of member maps $\pi|_{U_\alpha}:U_\alpha\to Q_\alpha\subseteq Q$ be as
in [[lem-gr-universal-development]] clauses (c)-(d), so that $Q$ is a
Hausdorff locally Euclidean smooth four-manifold with a smooth Lorentzian
metric $\bar g$, the sets $Q_\alpha$ are open and cover $Q$, and
$\bar j(\Sigma)\subseteq Q$ is the embedded initial surface. Then there is a
countable subset $D\subseteq Q$ with:

**(a)** $D\cap\bar j(\Sigma)$ is dense in $\bar j(\Sigma)$; and

**(b)** $D$ is dense in $Q$.

Moreover $D$ can be chosen of the following explicit form: with
$D_0:=S_0$ a countable dense subset of $\bar j(\Sigma)$, and having chosen
once at its first occurrence for every $x\in D_n$ a basis $(e_1(x),\dots,e_4(x))$ of $T_xQ$ and defined
$$V_x^{\mathrm{rat}}:=\Bigl\{\sum_{i=1}^4q_ie_i(x):\ q_i\in\mathbb Q\Bigr\},$$
one sets
$$D_{n+1}:=D_n\cup\bigl\{\exp_x(v):\ x\in D_n,\ v\in V_x^{\mathrm{rat}}\text{ timelike, with }\exp_x(v)\text{ defined}\bigr\},\qquad D:=\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb N}D_n.$$

quotes.quote: 1.1 (The set $D$.) Choose a countable dense subset $S_0\subseteq\bar j(\Sigma)$ ([L2]) and set $D_0:=S_0$. Recursively, given the countable set $D_n$, choose by Countable Choice a basis $(e_1(x),\dots,e_4(x))$ of $T_xQ$ at every newly added point, retaining all previously chosen bases, form $V_x^{\mathrm{rat}}$ as in the statement, and define $D_{n+1}$ by adding all points $\exp_x(v)$ with $x\in D_n$, $v\in V_x^{\mathrm{rat}}$ timelike and $\exp_x(v)$ defined. Dependent Choice supplies successive compatible choices of these basis assignments and sets. Each $D_{n+1}$ is countable, being the image of a subset of the countable set $D_n\times\mathbb Q^4$; hence $D:=\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb N}D_n$ is countable by [L6]. Since $D_0\subseteq D$, claim (a) holds. [L2, L6, construct]

1.2 (Chains of timelike chords, including the past direction.) Fix $p\in Q$ and a member $Q_\alpha$ containing it. In that member the complete flow of [L5] joins a point $z_0\in S:=\bar j(\Sigma)$ to $p$ with a parameter $t_1\in\mathbb R$. If $t_1=0$, then $p\in S$ and is already in the closure of $D_0$. Otherwise finitely many convex normal neighborhoods cover this compact flow segment; a sufficiently fine finite partition of the segment has each subsegment contained in one of those neighborhoods. Write the ordered endpoints along the flow from $S$ to $p$ as $z_0,\ldots,z_k=p$. The inverse velocity $w_i=v(z_{i-1},z_i)$ for each contained joining geodesic is timelike by [L4], using future chords when $t_1>0$ and past chords when $t_1<0$ (reverse the future-directed chord and use the time reversal of the geodesic). The recursion includes both future and past timelike vectors. [L1, L3, L4, L5, construct]

The recursion includes both future and past timelike vectors. [L1, L3, L4, L5, construct]

2.1 (Propagation of closure, without a stage-index assumption.) Work in $Q_\alpha$ and prove $z_i\in\overline{D\cap Q_\alpha}$ by induction. The case $i=0$ follows from the density of $D_0$ in $S$, since $S$ lies in every member. Suppose the claim holds for $z_{i-1}$, and prescribe any open neighborhood $O$ of $z_i$ within this member. The two-point inverse $v(q,z_i)$ is defined for $q$ close to $z_{i-1}$ in the convex neighborhood of step 1.2 and tends to the timelike vector $w_i$. Hence, for sufficiently close $q$, it is timelike. Choose such a $d\in D\cap Q_\alpha$ by the induction hypothesis. There is an open neighborhood of $v(d,z_i)$ in $T_dQ$ on which vectors remain timelike, the member geodesic remains defined to time one, and its exponential image lies in $O$, by openness and continuity of the member exponential. Choose a vector $u$ in the fixed rational span at $d$ in this neighborhood. Its quotient exponential equals its member exponential by uniqueness of the geodesic ODE and remains in $O$. As $d\in D_m$ for some $m$, the recursion gives $\exp_du\in D_{m+1}\subseteq D$. This proves that every such $O$ meets $D\cap Q_\alpha$, completing the induction. The exact inverse identity $\exp_d(v(d,z_i))=z_i$ has zero error; only approximation of this vector by $u$ contributes an endpoint error. [step 1.1, step 1.2, L3, L4, construct]

claim_evidence.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $Q$ and the member maps
$\pi|_{U_\alpha}:U_\alpha\to Q_\alpha\subseteq Q$ be as in
[[lem-gr-universal-development]] clauses (c)-(d): $Q$ is a Hausdorff locally
Euclidean smooth four-manifold with a smooth Lorentzian metric $\bar g$, the
open sets $Q_\alpha$ cover $Q$, and each $\pi|_{U_\alpha}$
is a diffeomorphism onto $Q_\alpha$. Let $D\subseteq Q$ be a countable dense
subset, as supplied by [[lem-gr-development-quotient-dense-set]]. Then $Q$ is
second countable ([[def-second-countable-space]]).

More precisely, choose one basis at each $d\in D$. In these coordinates let
$B_d(a,r)\subseteq T_dQ$ be the Euclidean open ball centered at
$a\in\mathbb Q^4$ with radius $r\in\mathbb Q_{>0}$, and let
$\mathcal E_d$ be the maximal exponential domain. Then
$$\mathcal B:=\{\exp_d(B_d(a,r)):d\in D, a\in\mathbb Q^4, r\in\mathbb Q_{>0}, B_d(a,r)\subseteq\mathcal E_d, \exp_d|_{B_d(a,r)}\text{ is a diffeomorphism onto an open subset of }Q\}$$
is a countable basis of the topology of $Q$.

Its first factor is an open neighborhood $V$ of $p$ in $Q$. Choose $d\in D\cap V$ by density. The inverse velocity $v(d,p)$ lies in $H_d$, where $\exp_d$ is a diffeomorphism onto an open subset of this member. Thus $H_d\cap\exp_d^{-1}(O)$ is an open neighborhood of $v(d,p)$ in $T_dQ$. claim_evidence.quote:
Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let
$(M,g,N,j,\psi)$ and $(M',g',N',j',\psi')$ be developments of the same data,
let $(U,\varphi)$ be a common subdevelopment in the sense of
[[def-gr-common-subdevelopment-and-corresponding-boundary]] clause (a), write
$\Sigma:=j(\Sigma)$, and let $p\in\partial U$ satisfy
$$J^-(p)\cap\partial U\cap J^+(\Sigma)=\{p\}$$
as in [[lem-gr-boundary-null-geodesic-segment]]. Then for every open
neighbourhood $W$ of $p$ in $M$ there exists $q\in I^+(p)$ with
$$J^-(q)\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)\subseteq W .$$

quotes.quote: 1.1 (Setup.) Let $\gamma:[0,\varepsilon]\to M$ be a future timelike curve with $\gamma(0)=p$ (it exists since every point of a time-oriented Lorentzian manifold has a future timelike curve). If the conclusion failed for every $q=\gamma(t)$, there would be a sequence $t_j\in(0,\varepsilon]$ with $t_j\to0$ and points $q_j\in J^-(\gamma(t_j))\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)\cap W^c$. [given, L1, choose]

4.1 ($q=p$, hence $q\in W$, contradiction.) If $q\in\partial U$, then $q\in J^-(p)\cap\partial U\cap J^+(\Sigma)=\{p\}$ by the exposed-point property, so $q=p\in W$, contradicting $q\in W^c$ of step 2.1. Hence $q\in U^c\setminus\partial U$; but $q\le p$ by step 3.1 and $q\in J^+(\Sigma)$ by step 2.1, contradicting step 1.2. Therefore the assumption of step 1.1 is false: for every sufficiently small $t$ one has $J^-(\gamma(t))\cap U^c\cap J^+(\Sigma)\subseteq W$, which is the assertion with $q:=\gamma(t)$. [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 1.2, contradiction] ∎
